values.name: module
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: A power module is a natural circulation light water reactor composed of a reactor core, a pressurizer, and two helical coil steam generators located in a common reactor pressure vessel that is housed in a compact cylindrical steel containment.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19

values.name: rating
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: Each power module has a rated thermal output of 160 megawatt thermal (MWt) and electrical output of 50 megawatt electric (MWe), yielding a total capacity of 600 MWe for 12 power modules.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19

values.name: pool
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: All the NuScale power modules are partially submerged in a common safety-related pool, which is also the ultimate heat sink for up to 12 power modules.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19

values.name: no-1E
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: NuScale does not contain safety-related Class 1E AC or DC electrical power systems.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19
source.locator: IV.E Absence of Safety-Related Class 1E AC or DC Electrical Power

values.name: no-power
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: NuScale has no safety-related functions that rely on electrical power. For example, the emergency core cooling system performs its safety function without reliance on safety-related electrical power or external sources of coolant inventory makeup.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19
source.locator: IV.E Absence of Safety-Related Class 1E AC or DC Electrical Power

values.name: eccs
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: The NuScale emergency core cooling system relies on natural circulation cooling of the reactor core by releasing the heated reactor coolant steam from the top of the reactor pressure vessel through three reactor vent valves into the containment vessel and returning the cooled condensed reactor coolant water to the reactor pressure vessel through two reactor recirculation valves.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19
source.locator: IV.C Emergency Core Cooling System Inadvertent Actuation Block Valve

values.name: eccs-valve
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: Each reactor vent valve and reactor recirculation valve consists of a first-of-a-kind arrangement of a main valve, an inadvertent actuation block (IAB) valve, a solenoid trip valve, and a solenoid reset valve.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19
source.locator: IV.C Emergency Core Cooling System Inadvertent Actuation Block Valve

values.name: iab
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: The IAB valve for each reactor vent valve and reactor recirculation valve is designed to close rapidly to prevent its corresponding emergency core cooling system main valve from opening when the reactor coolant system is at high pressure conditions.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19
source.locator: IV.C Emergency Core Cooling System Inadvertent Actuation Block Valve

values.name: sg
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: Damage to multiple steam generator tubes could disrupt natural circulation in the reactor coolant pathway and interfere with the decay heat removal system and the emergency core cooling system, which is relied upon to cool the reactor core in a NuScale power module.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19

values.name: cr
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: In a letter to the NRC, dated September 15, 2015, NuScale Power proposed that 6 licensed operators would operate up to 12 power modules from a single control room.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19

values.name: dhrs
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: Two trains of decay heat removal equipment are provided, one for each steam generator. Each train is capable of removing 100 percent of the decay heat load

source.title: K. Welter, J. N. Reyes Jr, A. Brigantic, Unique safety features and licensing requirements of the NuScale small modular reactor, Frontiers in Energy Research 11 (2023), doi:10.3389/fenrg.2023.1160150

values.name: dhrs-act
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: When responding to a design basis event and upon receipt of an actuation signal, the DHRS isolation valves open and the secondary system (main steam and feedwater) isolation valves close.

source.title: K. Welter, J. N. Reyes Jr, A. Brigantic, Unique safety features and licensing requirements of the NuScale small modular reactor, Frontiers in Energy Research 11 (2023), doi:10.3389/fenrg.2023.1160150

values.name: dhrs-pool
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: The DHRS condenser...is submerged in the reactor pool.

source.title: K. Welter, J. N. Reyes Jr, A. Brigantic, Unique safety features and licensing requirements of the NuScale small modular reactor, Frontiers in Energy Research 11 (2023), doi:10.3389/fenrg.2023.1160150

values.name: failsafe
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: valves that fail to their safe position on a loss of power, meaning that safety system operation is ensured without reliance on electrical power.

source.title: K. Welter, J. N. Reyes Jr, A. Brigantic, Unique safety features and licensing requirements of the NuScale small modular reactor, Frontiers in Energy Research 11 (2023), doi:10.3389/fenrg.2023.1160150

values.name: mps
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: When power is available, the systems are controlled via a dedicated safety-related module protection system (MPS), which monitors various plant conditions and actuates the safety systems if required.

source.title: K. Welter, J. N. Reyes Jr, A. Brigantic, Unique safety features and licensing requirements of the NuScale small modular reactor, Frontiers in Energy Research 11 (2023), doi:10.3389/fenrg.2023.1160150

values.name: pool-heat
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: The pool absorbs the decay heat from the modules and eventually begins to boil.

source.title: K. Welter, J. N. Reyes Jr, A. Brigantic, Unique safety features and licensing requirements of the NuScale small modular reactor, Frontiers in Energy Research 11 (2023), doi:10.3389/fenrg.2023.1160150

values.name: rxb
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: The NPMs are located below grade in a...Seismic Category I reactor building.

source.title: K. Welter, J. N. Reyes Jr, A. Brigantic, Unique safety features and licensing requirements of the NuScale small modular reactor, Frontiers in Energy Research 11 (2023), doi:10.3389/fenrg.2023.1160150

values.name: eccs-2rvv
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: The system is initiated by opening the two reactor vent valves at the top of the reactor pressure vessel (the pressurizer region) and the two fail-safe reactor recirculation valves

source.title: K. Welter, J. N. Reyes Jr, A. Brigantic, Unique safety features and licensing requirements of the NuScale small modular reactor, Frontiers in Energy Research 11 (2023), doi:10.3389/fenrg.2023.1160150

values.name: rxb-12
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: The NuScale reactor building is designed to hold up to 12 power modules.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19

values.name: pool-grade
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: The pool portion of the reactor building is located below grade.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19

values.name: bay-gallery
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: This issue is narrowly focused on the shielding walls between the reactor module bays and the reactor building steam gallery areas.

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19
source.locator: III.C Issues Not Resolved by the Design Certification

values.name: rz-map
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: design certification application Part 2, Tier 2, Chapter 12, Figure 12.3-1, ``Reactor Building Radiation Zone Map''

source.title: NuScale Small Modular Reactor Design Certification, final rule (10 CFR Part 52, Appendix G), 88 FR 3287, Federal Register Doc. 2023-00729, 2023-01-19

values.name: cnv-size
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: The reactor vessel is enclosed in a stainless steel containment vessel (CNV) that is nominally 76 ft tall and 19 ft in diameter.

source.title: K. Welter, J. N. Reyes Jr, A. Brigantic, Unique safety features and licensing requirements of the NuScale small modular reactor, Frontiers in Energy Research 11 (2023), doi:10.3389/fenrg.2023.1160150

values.name: bay-size
values.subject: NuScale US600
values.statement: Each NPM is operated in its own bay, immersed in a pool of water which is approximately 20 ft square by 53 ft deep (see Figure 3 ).

source.title: K. Welter, J. N. Reyes Jr, A. Brigantic, Unique safety features and licensing requirements of the NuScale small modular reactor, Frontiers in Energy Research 11 (2023), doi:10.3389/fenrg.2023.1160150
